instructions: Drives the Daylight app (sun, sky and view analysis of 3D building models) in the user's browser tab, or in a hidden instance when no tab is open (opening the app takes its session over). Start with app_state; read guide 'daylight', 'views', 'sets' or 'report' before interpreting or building on results. Conventions: models by letter A-D (design options sharing site, weather, time and settings; default the active one); building parts by USD prim path ('/' = all; model_tree finds them); times 'HH:MM' local standard time, dates YYYY-MM-DD; azimuth in degrees clockwise from true north; lengths in m, areas in m², model coordinates Z up. `analysis` picks daylight (default), views (the View analysis: what each element sees) or combined (the Combined tab: saved sets' results joined per element); each has its own roles, settings, runs and results. Changed inputs make results stale: run. Steps that outlast a call answer 'running' or 'generating': call again. Quote numbers only from tool output; sections cut the views only, never runs or results.

tools.name: app_state
tools.title: App state
tools.description: Snapshot of the app: call it first and whenever the user may have changed something. JSON: the tab (UI or hidden, visible); per model A-D its name, file, variant choices, load state and problems, meshes by role, faces, run status and result freshness (fresh, stale, running); display (as set_display takes it); every setting (as update_settings takes it) and the problems that would stop a run; viewAnalysis (settings, field grid, roles, runs, problems); saved views; reports; sets (summary, and per model a status: done = a result for its inputs now is kept this session); combined views (meaning, inputs each model misses).

tools.name: guide
tools.title: Read a guide
tools.description: Reference text (markdown): read the one you need before acting on results. daylight: each result column (unit, aggregation), time modes, area weighting, assumptions, what is not computed (daylight factor, VSC, DA/sDA/UDI, glare, PV yield) and how to derive common checks (EN 17037, BRE sun hours, PV potential, comparing options). views: the View analysis' columns, settings and limits. sets: analysis sets, kept results and combined views. report: the ReportSpec with examples, before save_report. kit-ui: the design system the reports follow.

tools.name: site_info
tools.title: Site and sun
tools.description: The site and its sun: place, coordinates, time zone (standard time, no daylight saving), north, weather source, the EPW header (station, km away, leap year) with its monthly digest (sunshine hours; GHI, DNI, DHI in kWh/m²) and the 8 nearest weather stations (title, km: pass a title as update_settings weather.station). Per date: sunrise, sunset, day length and the sun's altitude and azimuth at the given hours. Dates default to the time setting's (annual: 21 Mar, 21 Jun, 21 Dec); hours to every full hour of daylight.

tools.name: update_settings
tools.title: Update settings
tools.description: Change the inputs every model shares (the Location, Time, Simulation, Weather and View settings panels, the Results panel's colours and charts). Only given fields change; reset sections go back to their defaults first. Changed inputs make results stale: run. site: query geocodes a name, locate asks the browser for the user's position (a move picks the nearest station). view: the View analysis' inputs. viz: one quantity's colour scale and problem range lo..hi (shared by every view, chart, shot, PDF, results and find_critical); library adds or removes gradients. Returns the settings, the View analysis' field grid and the problems a run would report.

reset.description: Sections back to their defaults, first: sim (all but north), time, and the View settings' view-field (fov, gaze, cell), view-eye (sides, on, offset), view-distance (far, reach) and view-ground (the rest).

query.description: Place name or address to geocode (first match; the others come back as alternatives).

locate.description: true: the user's position as the browser knows it (it asks the user first; the reply says why it failed, e.g. in the hidden instance).

mode.description: annual, instant (date and hour) or range (from, to, step).

date.description: Instant: the date (its year is not used).

from.description: Range: first date and daily start.

to.description: Range: last date and daily end.

mode.description: physical (default), or ladybug: RadiationStudy's opaque black scene (no illuminance, transmission or reflections).

quantities.description: Quantities computed; each gives a column per side, e.g. illuminance_front.

sides.description: Receiving side: front (where the normal points), back, or both.

on.description: Sensors on each face (centroid) or vertex.

north.description: Degrees counter-clockwise from the model's +Y to true north (90: -X is north).

transmission.description: Glass, screens and trees pass light by their transmittance (physical).

bounceSamples.description: Paths per sensor with reflections; noise falls as 1/sqrt(samples).

offset.description: Sensor offset along the normal, m.

cullBackfaces.description: Occluders block only from their front.

selfOcclude.description: Receivers block rays too (default on); off: no receiver casts shade.

view.description: View settings panel: the View analysis' run inputs (its roles: set_roles analysis views).

fov.description: Field [width, from, to] in degrees: width 1 to 180 about each face's normal (a window; default [120, -70, 50]) or 360 all around (azimuth from north); elevations -90 to 90, from below to; [360, 0, 0]: one ring of level rays (the 2D isovist).

gaze.description: Window fields only: level (default) centres the field on the normal turned level, as a person looks; normal tilts it with the face.

cell.description: Degrees per ray cell (the panel offers 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5; 1 for thin or far targets); at most 2^20 rays per element.

sides.description: Looking side: front, back or both.

on.description: Eyes on each face (centroid) or vertex.

offset.description: Eye offset along the normal, m (1.2 seated, 1.6 standing above a floor grid).

far.description: What an open ray counts as and the cap of every distance, m, more than 0.1 (interiors: 20 to 50).

reach.description: Reach distances: '' none, 'en17037' (6, 20 and 50 m) or up to 8 distances in m separated by commas: the share of the field that sees at least that far.

virtualGround.description: A plane at the lowest point (or groundZ) ends downward rays as ground.

groundZ.description: Virtual ground height, m; null: the lowest point of the run's meshes.

transmission.description: Rays pass glass and count what lies behind; off: windows block.

cullBackfaces.description: Obstructions block only from their front.

source.description: station (an EPW station), pvgis (the PVGIS typical year here), upload (an EPW file) or clear-sky (Ineichen, no file).

station.description: A station title from site_info; sets source station.

file.description: Absolute path of an .epw file on this computer; sets source upload.

turbidity.description: Clear sky: Linke turbidity (2 very clear to 7 polluted).

viz.description: One quantity's colour scale and problem range (its front and back columns share them), and the gradient library.

quantity.description: A Daylight quantity (radiation, direct, diffuse, irradiance, illuminance, sunhours), a View analysis one (sky, ground, obstruction, obstruction_total, glazing, volume, area, distance, distance_min, reach_<D>, a target group) or combined_<id>; default the shown column's.

gradient.description: Gradient key: inferno, magma, plasma, viridis, cividis, turbo, ladybug, greys, blues, greens, oranges, purples, or a library one (an unknown key: the quantity's default).

scaling.description: How values spread between min and max: linear, log (equal ratios, equal steps), sqrt (stretches the low end), square (the high end), equalised (each colour covers as many elements).

min.description: Legend minimum, the quantity's unit; null: the data's over every model.

max.description: Legend maximum, the quantity's unit; null: the data's over every model.

lo.description: Problem range: values under it are painted belowColour and count as problems; null: no lower bound.

hi.description: Problem range: values over it are painted aboveColour and count as problems; null: no upper bound.

belowColour.description: Colour under the range, '#rrggbb', every quantity's (default #0000ff).

aboveColour.description: Colour over the range, '#rrggbb', every quantity's (default #ff0000).

reset.description: Applied first: 'scale' restores gradient, scaling, min and max; 'range' clears the problem range and both colours.

library.description: Gradients added, changed or removed first (the gradient editor), each by key; a preset key changes or restores that preset.

positions.description: Where each stop sits, ascending 0 to 1; default evenly spaced.

remove.description: true: remove it (a preset: back as built in).

charts.description: Results panel charts, in order: a new id adds one (kind needed), an existing id changes the given fields; {id, remove: true} deletes an added chart, {id, reset: true} restores one. 'hist' and 'curve' are built in. Report charts: save_report.

id.description: 'hist', 'curve' or an id of your own.

kind.description: histogram (area share per bin), curve (area share at or below each value) or parts (a bar per model for each prim).

column.description: Result column; default the shown one.

models.description: Models drawn; default every model with a result.

parts.description: Prims: histogram and curve count the receivers under them; parts draws a row each (up to 24).

range.description: Value axis: relative (the colour scale, default), absolute (the data's) or [min, max].

markers.description: Statistics marked (with one model drawn; the curve has no mean).

height.description: Height at a width of 320 (default 200, curve 170).

metric.description: parts: each bar's value; below, within and above are problem-range area shares (default mean).

tools.name: open_model
tools.title: Open a model
tools.description: Open a model from this computer (the Model panel's pickers). paths: one folder (a USD scene with its assets; its top-level USD file opens) or files (.usd, .usda, .usdc, .usdz, .glb, .gltf with .bin and textures, .obj with .mtl). model: the slot to open into, replacing what it holds; default the active slot if empty, else a new one (four at most). A lone mesh becomes the receiver; otherwise every mesh starts ignored: set_roles. Returns the letter, name, units, mesh count, top prims and load problems. A big model may answer 'running': poll app_state, do not open it again.

paths.description: Absolute paths: one folder, or the model's files.

model.description: Slot to open into; default the active slot if empty, else a new one.

tools.name: remove_model
tools.title: Remove a model
tools.description: Remove a model (the x on its tab): its view, roles, result and any job on its way. The other models keep their letters. Refused for the last model and while a model is loading.

tools.name: model_tree
tools.title: Model prim tree
tools.description: Browse a model's prims to name building parts: the prims below path, depth levels deep, each with type, children, meshes and triangles under it and their role (receiver, shade, none, mixed; shade false where its receivers cast no shade), visibility, lock and variant sets with the selected variant. query searches the whole stage instead: words match names, 'type:Mesh' filters by type, e.g. 'type:Mesh roof'. At most limit prims; the reply says when there are more.

model.description: Model letter; default the active model.

path.description: Prim to list below; default '/' (the stage root).

query.description: Search the whole stage instead, e.g. 'type:Mesh roof'.

tools.name: set_roles
tools.title: Set mesh roles
tools.description: Set the role of every mesh at or under the given prims (the Model panel's role buttons). Daylight: receiver (gets results, casts shade; shade false: measures without casting shade, e.g. a sensor grid in a room), shade (only blocks: neighbours, trees) or none. analysis views: receiver, obstruction (only blocks the view) or target with a group (its share of the view is the column <group>_front). Instanced meshes only shade or are ignored. reset: every mesh back to its role at load first. A role change clears the result. Returns the role counts, the meshes changed and the paths that matched nothing.

model.description: Model letter; default the active model.

analysis.description: Whose roles: Daylight's (default) or the View analysis'.

reset.description: true: every mesh back to its role at load first (no groups, every receiver casting shade).

paths.description: Prim paths; every mesh at or under each ('/' = all). Needed unless reset.

role.description: Daylight: receiver, shade or none; View analysis: receiver, obstruction, target or none.

group.description: With role target: the target group, the result's column (e.g. 'park' gives park_front).

shade.description: Role receiver only: false = gets results but casts no shade; true = casts shade (default for a new receiver).

tools.name: set_visibility
tools.title: Set visibility
tools.description: Change what the 3D view shows and what can be picked (the prim tree's eye and lock, the H keys). View only: hidden meshes still run by their role; nothing is saved. Applied in order: showAll, hide, show, isolate (show only these), lock and unlock (picking in the view), select ([] clears). Returns the hidden, locked and selected paths.

model.description: Model letter; default the active model.

lock.description: Prims the user can no longer pick in the view.

select.description: Prims to select ([] clears the selection).

tools.name: set_geometry
tools.title: Change model geometry
tools.description: Change what is drawn and simulated (the prim tree's variant column, the Model panel's subdivision). variant: switch a variant set on a prim (sets and values from model_tree). subdivision: refine catmullClark and loop meshes; without paths one level for every model (0 control cage, the default; -1 the authored schemes up to 2; 1 to 3), with paths that level for the meshes under them ('model' restores the model's), which keep it unless override. Roles are kept by path, new meshes start ignored, the result clears. Returns mesh and role counts; a slow re-read may answer 'running': poll app_state.

model.description: Model letter; default the active model.

paths.description: Prims whose meshes get the level; default every model as a whole.

override.description: No paths: true, the level also for meshes with their own (file or paths); false, theirs again. Default: unchanged.

tools.name: get_materials
tools.title: Get materials
tools.description: A model's Materials table: 'default' (surfaces without a material; opaque, reflectance 0.2), 'glass' (glass without numbers; transmittance 0.64) and each material bound to a receiver or shade, by path. Per row: kind (opaque, glass, porous), reflectance rho and transmittance tau (0 to 1, visible light, also used for energy), source (derived, default, edited, unread) and any warning, plus the presets edit_material takes. The values count only in physical mode with transmission (tau) or bounces (rho); otherwise every surface is opaque and black.

model.description: Model letter; default the active model.

tools.name: edit_material
tools.title: Edit a material
tools.description: Override one row of a model's Materials table (its kind select and boxes): a preset, or kind, rho and/or tau (a kind change keeps the surface's albedo; glass reflects by angle, so its rho is 0). reset: the row back to its derived or default values; reset without material: every edit of the model. Values outside the core's ranges are adjusted at run time with a warning (get_materials). Edits last until the model is opened again and make results stale where they count (physical mode with transmission or bounces). Returns the row.

model.description: Model letter; default the active model.

material.description: 'default', 'glass' or a material path; left out with reset: every edit of the model.

preset.description: Preset name from get_materials, e.g. 'Brick', 'Double low-e', 'Opening (no glazing)'.

reset.description: true: back to the derived or default values.

tools.name: run
tools.title: Run the simulation
tools.description: Run an analysis for every model with a receiver, with the inputs now (its Run button): one GPU job per model, in turn; joins a batch already running. Waits up to wait seconds, then answers 'running' (call again to keep waiting). Returns per model its status (done, failed with the reason, queued, running, stale, no receiver, not run), run time and the shown column's mean, P10 and P90; or the problems that stopped it (fix them with update_settings, set_roles or edit_material). cancel stops the batch; finished models keep their results. Saved sets run with run_set.

analysis.description: Which analysis runs: Daylight (default) or the View analysis.

cancel.description: true: stop the running batch instead.

tools.name: results
tools.title: Result statistics
tools.description: Area-weighted statistics of one column per model: elements, area (m²), min, P10, median, mean, P90, max, total (value x area), the area shares (%) below, within and above the problem range, and below and at or above each threshold. A whole-model row, then rows by mesh, by parts (each prim in paths) or by facing (N, E, S, W, up, down). The first model is the reference: the others carry differences to it. Also the unit, meaning, freshness and run provenance. From analysis daylight or views (the last runs), set (a saved set's kept results, not opened) or analysis combined with id (a combined view; missing input sets run first).

analysis.description: Whose results: Daylight (default), the View analysis, or a combined view (with id).

id.description: With analysis 'combined': the combined view (app_state combined).

set.description: A saved set's kept results instead (app_state sets), without opening it.

models.description: Models; the first is the reference the others are compared to. Default every model with a result.

column.description: Result column, e.g. 'sunhours_front' or 'sky_front'; default the shown one (a set's: its own; a combined view: its own).

by.description: Rows per receiver mesh, per prim in paths, or per side faced; default parts with paths, else mesh.

paths.description: Prim paths: a row each with by parts; with mesh or facing, only the receivers under them.

thresholds.description: Values in the column's unit, e.g. [1.5, 3, 4]; each gives the area shares below and at or above it.

wait.description: Combined: seconds to wait for the input sets missing a result to run (default 40; 0: quote what there is, run nothing).

tools.name: find_critical
tools.title: Find critical areas
tools.description: Where a model does worst in one column: its elements under lo or over hi (default the problem range, update_settings viz), grouped by receiver mesh and the side they face, largest problem area first. Per group: mesh, facing, elements, area (m²) and its share of that side, mean and worst value, centre, box and normal (m, model coordinates), a camera view from the side it faces and near, the cutaway (m) that clears what stands in front: pass them to screenshot or set_camera (another image shape: box and normal as frame). Also the model's problem area and share. Needs a fresh result.

model.description: Model letter; default the active model.

analysis.description: Whose result: Daylight's (default) or the View analysis'.

column.description: Result column; default the shown one.

lo.description: Elements under it are problems (the column's unit); default the problem range's.

hi.description: Elements over it are problems (the column's unit); default the problem range's.

tools.name: set_display
tools.title: Set the display
tools.description: Change what the views show (the app bar, Results panel, Display and Section menus). Only given fields change; none touches a run or makes results stale. analysis: the tab shown and whose column and colourBy change (combined: id picks the view). Also the active model, labels (values on the surfaces) and their look, display mode, sky, highlight (value ranges kept bright), sun path (sunPath, sunScale, sunAround), the View analysis' fieldPreview, theme, split, link, auto run, and section: clipping planes and boxes replacing the whole section ({planes: [], boxes: []} clears it). Returns the display, section boxes as footprints.

analysis.description: The tab shown, and whose column and colourBy change: Daylight, View analysis or Combined.

id.description: With analysis 'combined': the combined view (app_state combined).

active.description: Active model (the Model and Materials panels, Views and Download act on it).

colourBy.description: value (result colours) or plain (the model's own look).

labels.description: Write each visible element's value on the surfaces (coloured by value only).

labelScale.description: The labels' size over the default; shots too.

labelSpacing.description: Their cells over the default: fewer labels.

labelLayout.description: spot: on their own face or point.

labelShow.description: extremes: the 10 highest and lowest in view; problem: outside the problem range.

labelColour.description: Their text colour without the box.

display.description: How the views draw the model: shaded (its materials) or plain grey, with every edge (-wire) or the selection's (-selwire), or wireframe; result colours show in each.

sky.description: Behind the model: none (the theme's colour; white in shots) or an HDRI sky that also lights it; result colours stay the legend's.

highlight.description: Value ranges [lo, hi] in the column's unit kept bright, the rest faded (as selected histogram bars); null or [] clears; a run clears it.

sunPath.description: Show the sun path around the model.

sunScale.description: Sun path size over the fitted one.

sunAround.description: Prims of the active model the sun path stands on and encloses; null or []: the whole model.

fieldPreview.description: The View analysis' field preview: the field each eye traces, drawn on the receivers (View analysis tab).

scale.description: Glyph size over the fitted one (1 = fitted).

around.description: Only on the receivers at or under these prims; null or []: every receiver.

theme.description: App theme; auto follows the system.

split.description: Two or three views side by side or stacked (four: 2 x 2).

link.description: Linked cameras: every view follows the active one.

section.description: Clipping planes and boxes (model coordinates, m, Z up), replacing the whole section. A point shows when every plane keeps it, no outside box holds it and, with inside boxes, one does.

on.description: false: the planes and boxes stay but cut nothing (default true); send the whole section (app_state display.section) with it.

planes.description: Planes, each keeping the side its normal points to.

point.description: A point on the plane [x, y, z].

normal.description: Towards the side kept [x, y, z]; [0, 0, -1] keeps what is below.

boxes.description: Vertical prisms: by footprint with bottom and top, by box, or round prims.

keep.description: inside: show only what is in it; outside: cut it away.

footprint.description: 4 corners [x, y] in order round it.

box.description: Or a box, e.g. a find_critical group's.

rotation.description: With box: degrees counter-clockwise seen from above, about its vertical centre line.

paths.description: Or round what is drawn at or under these prims of the active model, square to the model axes (loose round turned prims: give a footprint for a tight cut).

margin.description: With box or paths: added on every side, m (default box 0, paths 1 % of their diagonal; a flat find_critical box needs one).

tools.name: set_camera
tools.title: Set the camera
tools.description: Move a model's 3D view; the user sees it (with linked cameras every view follows). Give one of: view, an exact camera from tool output; camera, a stage camera path or saved view name; or frame, the prims or box to fit, seen from direction at elevation degrees and fitted to aspect (the width/height of the screenshot you plan). Nothing given frames the whole model. Returns the view, a description (from which side and bearing, elevation, distance in m) and, for frame, near: the cutaway (m) that clears what stands in front. To only capture an image, pass view or frame to screenshot instead.

model.description: Model letter; default the active model.

view.description: An exact camera in the viewer's world coordinates (stage units, Y up): copy it from tool output.

camera.description: A stage camera path or a saved view name.

frame.description: What to fit: {paths}, or {box, normal} (a find_critical group's); {}: the whole model.

normal.description: Direction the framed surfaces face [x, y, z] (direction auto).

direction.description: Frame: where the camera stands, true compass ('S' sees south-facing surfaces); top: plan, north up; auto (default) faces the framed surfaces, a closed shape from the SW.

elevation.description: Frame: degrees above the horizon (default 20; negative looks up); with auto above the surfaces' own tilt (a closed shape at 35).

aspect.description: Frame: width/height to fit; default the view's.

tools.name: save_view
tools.title: Save a view
tools.description: Save the model's current camera in the Views menu under name (this session; it serves every view), or remove the saved view of that name. To save a camera not applied yet, call set_camera first. Returns the saved view and the list. Report cameras are a report's view blocks (save_report), not saved views.

model.description: Model whose camera is saved; default the active model.

remove.description: true: remove the saved view of that name.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.title: Take a screenshot
tools.description: Render model views as JPEG images of any size, also while the tab is hidden; never moves the user's camera. Each model from its current camera, from view, or framed with frame (as set_camera, fitted to width/height); near cuts away what is closer to the eye (find_critical gives it). analysis, id, column, colourBy, labels, display, highlight, sunPath, sunAround, fieldPreview, grid and section apply to this shot only, as set_display takes them (section null: none). 16 to 8192 px a side, at most 8 MP; images come at most 1568 px on the long side, recompressed past ~800 KB a reply. Per model one image and a text: camera, colour scale, size and section.

models.description: Models, an image each; default the active one.

view.description: An exact camera for every image, as set_camera's.

frame.description: What to fit, as set_camera's; {}: the whole model.

normal.description: Direction the framed surfaces face [x, y, z] (direction auto).

projection.description: Frame: projection; default the view's current one.

near.description: Cutaway: geometry nearer the eye than this, m, is not drawn.

analysis.description: Whose results the shot shows: Daylight, View analysis or Combined; default the tab shown.

id.description: With analysis 'combined': the combined view (app_state combined).

column.description: Result column to colour by; default the shown one.

colourBy.description: value (result colours) or plain (the model's own look).

labels.description: Write each visible element's value on the surfaces (coloured by value only); default the Display menu's, in its look.

sunPath.description: Draw the sun path; default as shown.

sunAround.description: As set_display, in each model shot; default as shown.

grid.description: Draw the ground grid; default as shown.

section.description: This shot's section, in set_display's section form (checked as there); null: none; default the views' own.

tools.name: get_report
tools.title: Get a report
tools.description: One stored report's full spec (app_state lists the ids) with its updated (pass it to save_report when replacing), whether a PDF exists, and whether it is ready to generate or what differs (a model not open, another variant, a stale result: open_model, set_geometry, set_roles and run restore them). setup: the Daylight setup the save recorded (per model its receiver and shade counts, the sim and time settings, the column), which generating opens first.

tools.name: save_report
tools.title: Save a report
tools.description: Create or replace a report from a ReportSpec: read guide 'report' first. One model: a report on that option; 2 to 4: a comparison (the first is the reference). Blocks: text quoting numbers from tool output, charts, views (a camera from find_critical or set_camera, with near, aspect and a section) and tables. Validated (each problem names its path, e.g. blocks[3].caption) and stored with the current Daylight setup, which generating opens first. Replacing takes the updated from get_report: refused when the user changed the report since. Returns id, updated and readiness; then generate_report.

spec.description: The ReportSpec, as described in guide 'report'.

updated.description: When replacing: the spec's updated time from get_report.

tools.name: delete_report
tools.title: Delete a report
tools.description: Delete a stored report with its PDF; it leaves the app's Reports menu. Cannot be undone. Refused while its PDF is being generated or is open in another program (the user closes it first).

tools.name: generate_report
tools.title: Generate report PDF
tools.description: Build a stored report as a PDF: its setup opened on the Daylight tab, models without a result run, figures drawn from the results (one image per view block and model, on the shared scale), laid out in the kit-report format and printed with headless Chrome or Edge. Refused with the reason when not ready (a model not open, another file or variant). Waits up to 40 s, then answers 'generating': call again. Returns the PDF path, a link, pages, bytes and fonts (fallback should be empty); then read it back, or ask the user to check it.

tools.name: download_result
tools.title: Download the result
tools.description: Save a model's result as a file in the browser's downloads folder (the Download menu; the model becomes active): USD (usdz, usda, usdc, usd), glTF (glb, gltf) or OBJ, receivers coloured by the analysis' shown column; every format but OBJ also holds each column as values. mode, USD only: replace (colours instead of the receivers' materials, default) or variants (a 'daylight' variant set per receiver on a flattened stage). A big model may answer 'running': the file lands by itself, do not call again. Downloads from a background tab can trip the browser's automatic-downloads block: the reply says so.

model.description: Model letter; default the active model.

analysis.description: Whose result: Daylight's (default) or the View analysis'.

mode.description: USD only: colours replace the materials, or a variant set per result.

tools.name: save_set
tools.title: Save an analysis set
tools.description: Save an analysis' whole setup under a name (the Sets menu's Save), stored for every client: per open model an entry linked to it (letter and file) with its roles and Materials edits, plus the run settings (daylight: sim, time, site and weather; views: view), north, the column shown, the colours, charts and subdivision level. roles and settings change the set only, not the app (open_set applies a set). id replaces a set of the same analysis. Returns the set and its status per model.

analysis.description: The set's analysis; default the set's (with id), else the tab shown's (daylight on the Combined tab).

id.description: A set's id to replace (app_state sets); left out: a new set.

roles.description: Role changes for the set only, applied in order to the app's roles now, as set_roles takes them.

model.description: Model letter; default the active model.

role.description: Daylight: receiver, shade, none; View analysis: receiver, obstruction, target, none.

shade.description: Role receiver: whether they cast shade.

group.description: Role target: its group (the column, e.g. park_front).

settings.description: Run settings for the set only, as update_settings takes them: sim and time (Daylight) or view (View analysis).

column.description: The column the set shows and run_set quotes; default the analysis' shown one.

colourBy.description: Colouring when opened; default the analysis' now.

tools.name: open_set
tools.title: Open an analysis set
tools.description: Apply a saved set to the app and show its tab (the Sets menu's Open): its settings, colours, charts and subdivision level, and per open model its own entry's roles and Materials edits (the entry of its letter and file; when that letter shows another file, the entry's file reopened in another slot). An entry never goes to another model: one without keeps its roles (copy_set makes it a set), an entry whose file is not open waits (notOpen). A result kept this session for the same inputs comes back without a run. Returns per model the entry it took, how, and the paths matched.

tools.name: copy_set
tools.title: Copy an analysis set to another model
tools.description: Make a new set of one entry of a saved set for another open model, then save and open it (the Sets fold-out's Copy to model): the entry's roles where the model has the same prim paths (its other meshes get none), its Materials edits of the material paths the model has, and everything else as it is. The set copied stays. Returns the new set, the roles and material edits matched and the meshes left without a role.

to.description: The open model the new set is for.

from.description: The set's entry to copy (its letter in the set); needed when the set has several.

name.description: The new set's name; default '<set name> for <file>'.

tools.name: rename_set
tools.title: Rename a set or combined view
tools.description: Rename a saved set or combined view for every client; its id and contents stay, so combined views that take a set keep it. Returns the id, the old name and the new one.

id.description: Set or combined view id (app_state sets, combined).

tools.name: run_set
tools.title: Run an analysis set
tools.description: Run a saved set in the background without opening it (the Combined tab's Sets panel): per open model with its own entry, the model as the set makes it, one job at a time while neither analysis runs; a set of another subdivision level runs only once opened. Results are kept this session (open_set, results with set and combined views find them; the same inputs never run twice). Default: the models without a result or failed. Waits up to wait seconds, then answers 'running': call again. Returns per model its status and the set's column mean, P10 and P90.

models.description: Models to run; default those without a result for the set.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for the runs (default 40; 0: answer at once).

tools.name: delete_set
tools.title: Delete a set or combined view
tools.description: Delete a saved set or combined view for every client; cannot be undone. A set's kept results stay this session; combined views that took the set as an input then miss it (the reply names them). A combined view's input sets stay.

id.description: Set or combined view id (app_state sets, combined).

tools.name: save_combined
tools.title: Save a combined view
tools.description: Create or replace a combined view (the Combined tab's editor): per element one value from up to 8 inputs, each a saved set's column transformed by fn (raw; normalise or invert to 0..1 over lo..hi, default every model's range; log10; threshold: 1 at or above lo; band: 1 within lo..hi), weighted, then joined by op (weighted mean or sum, min, max, product with weights as powers). meshes limits an input to prims; inputs must run on the same elements. preview: show it without storing it. Read guide 'sets' first. Returns the view in words and the inputs each model misses (run_set, or results with analysis combined, runs them).

id.description: A combined view's id to replace; left out: a new one.

op.description: How the inputs join per element.

inputs.description: The inputs, each a saved set's column.

lo.description: normalise, invert, band: lower bound; threshold: the threshold (default mid-range).

meshes.description: Prims it covers; default every receiver.

look.description: Its colours until the Results panel sets its own.

preview.description: true: show it on the Combined tab without storing it, until a save, an edit in the app or leaving the tab.
